data.name: Namish
data.gender_notes: Namish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Namish’ which means ‘desire’ or ‘wish’, this name is associated with the act of naming a child to give it an identity and a purpose in life. In Hindu mythology, it is believed that a child's name holds a significant influence on its future and character. The name Namish carries the meaning “Desire, Wish, Intention” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Namish usually hope their child will grow to embody desire, wish, intention and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May your desires and intentions be fulfilled.
data.etymology: Namish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Desire, Wish, Intention.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Namish total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Namish also holds great spiritual significance as it is believed that the child's soul enters the body at the time of birth with the name given by the parents. The name is seen as a divine gift and a manifestation of the parents' profound desire and longing for their child. It is believed that the name given to a child by the parents shapes its karmic destiny and influences its spiritual growth. The name Namish, in particular, is believed to inspire the child to pursue its deepest desires and dreams, and to live a purposeful and meaningful life.
